description:
LIVE WRONG ANSWER at 788c0c21f, found while grounding fz-kdt.118's soundness
obligation. Independent of fz-kdt.118 (byte-identical before and after it):
this is fz-kdt.107's residue with the grounding path attached, and it REFUTES
the premise fz-kdt.118 was asked to prove.

REPRO (8 lines, no protocol, no annotation, no stdlib):

  defmodule Pipeline do
    fn apply_twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: apply_twice(f, x)
  end

  fn main() do
    dbg(Pipeline.run(fn (n) -> n + 1 end, 10))
    dbg(Pipeline.run(fn (n) -> n * 3 end, 10))
  end

Means 12 then 90. Prints 12 then 12, on run + interp + AOT alike. Delete the
forwarding hop (call apply_twice from main directly) and it is correct.

THE MECHANISM, end to end:
- A function that only FORWARDS a closure generalizes its arrow position, so
  one shared body serves both lambdas: `key Pipeline.run/2[fp[F] (a0_p0) ->
  a0_r, fp[int] int]`.
- A function that INVOKES the closure specializes on the literal:
  `key Pipeline.apply_twice/2[fp[F] closure[main/0#lambda@135-154/1](), ...]`
  twice, once per lambda.
- `run/2`'s single callsite names both. `runtime_type_test_envelope`
  (types/mod.rs:1519, line 1522 `descr.funcs = Descr::fun_top().funcs`) erases
  both literals to fun_top, so `discriminating_inputs` finds nothing to test
  and the plan compiles to an unconditional `root -> o0`: arm 1 is emitted and
  unreachable, every value goes to arm 0.
- Arm 0's body direct-calls ITS OWN closure. The chain is specialization input
  type -> `resolve_closure_call` (jobs/semantic.rs:727) -> a one-target
  CallSiteSummary -> `closure_callee_demand` (jobs/runtime_demand.rs:2990) ->
  `CallableDemand.targets.len() == 1` -> `exact_direct_callable_layout`
  (jobs/transport.rs:901) -> `TransportCarrier::Absent` ->
  `materialize_closure_call_edge` (jobs/artifact.rs:1392) -> CallEdge::Direct.
  The sibling's lambda never runs.

WITH CAPTURES IT CORRUPTS MEMORY, not just results. Same shape, closures
capturing `a = 1` / `b = 100`: interp prints 8 then 107 (arm 0's body `x + a`
executed against arm 1's capture record 100 -> 7 + 100); run/AOT hard-abort in
`fz_ref_load_int: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(13), found: ValueKind(4) }`
(runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:246), because a grounded callable's ABI is its
capture lanes (jobs/artifact.rs:2088) and the surviving specialization's
param_reprs are typed to ITS capture layout.

WHAT IT REFUTES: fz-kdt.118's named open question was "a callable position
erased to fun_top by runtime_type_test_envelope is always invoked indirectly at
the surviving body". FALSE. It is invoked indirectly whenever the position is
generalized (`fp[va5] a5`), which is what the stdlib's recursive
reduce_cont/reduce_step cycle happens to force -- and that is the only reason
Enumerable.reduce is clean. A non-recursive one-hop helper gets no such
protection.

WHY fz-kdt.118 DOES NOT CAUSE IT AND A CARVE-OUT WOULD NOT CURE IT: here the
two arms' observable surfaces are IDENTICAL, so containment is mutual, the
drop's strictness keeps both, and fz-kdt.118 changes nothing (verified:
byte-identical output before and after). Dropping a runtime-indistinguishable
arm never changes a routing -- the plan asks no question that separates the
group, so one member receives everything either way -- so a "do not drop when
the callable position is grounded" carve-out would preserve a dead arm and
change no answer. The cure is upstream: either the callsite must not offer
arms it cannot separate, or a body specialized on a closure literal must not
ground a direct call to it unless every caller proves that literal is what
arrives.

BOUNDARY (controls measured):
- invoker called directly from main, two lambdas -> CORRECT
- one forwarding hop between main and the invoker -> WRONG
- forwarder carries an arrow @spec -> WRONG (annotation is not the cause)
- forwarder is a protocol boundary -> WRONG
- closure invoked IN the generalized body -> CORRECT (stays indirect)
- three lambdas -> all three answers are the first lambda's
- an extra :a/:b argument beside the closure -> CORRECT (the plan now has a
  question to ask -- which is exactly fz-kdt.119's direction)

Probe programs: session scratchpad hunt/ (s2.fz, c1-c8.fz, t1.fz).
Known-red gate: `compiler2_forwarded_closures_are_not_replaced_by_their_sibling`
in drive_test.rs, #[ignore]d with this ticket's name.
title: P1: a closure forwarded through one generalized hop is silently replaced by its sibling
